standard_prerequisites.name: The principal divisor of a rational function on a proper curve over a field is zero, and pushforward along an alteration
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter chow.tex, labels lemma-curve-principal-divisor (proof line 3298) and lemma-proper-pushforward-alteration (proof line 3302)
standard_prerequisites.use: The first supplies the vanishing of the multiplicity in the dimension k case through the proper integral curve W_eta over the residue field of the generic point, and the second handles the case where the image has the same dimension as W.

core_obligations: Unwind the definition: it is enough to treat a locally finite family of integral closed subschemes W_j of delta-dimension k + 1 with rational functions f_j and to show that p_*(sum i_{j,*} div(f_j)) is rationally equivalent to zero on Y (proof lines 3225-3238).

Reduce to a single W: distribute the pushforward over the locally finite sum, take W'_j to be the image of p composed with i_j, note the W'_j are locally finite in Y, and conclude that it suffices to show for each j that p_* i_{j,*} div(f_j) is zero or a divisor of a rational function on W'_j (proof lines 3240-3250).

Split into three cases according to dim_delta(W'): if dim_delta(W') < k the pushforward vanishes automatically; if dim_delta(W') = k, use that the fibre W_eta over the generic point of W' is a proper integral curve over K = kappa(eta) whose closed points correspond bijectively to the integral subschemes Z of W of dimension k mapping onto W', so the multiplicity of [W'] in (p')_* div(f) equals the multiplicity of [Spec(K)] in c_* div(f_eta), which is zero by the principal divisor lemma; and if dim_delta(W') = k + 1 the alteration lemma gives (p')_* div(f) = div(g) for some g in R(W')^* (proof lines 3252-3304).
proof_roadmap: Unwind rational equivalence into a locally finite sum of divisors of rational functions (proof lines 3225-3238).
Push the sum forward, observe the image family is locally finite, and reduce to one integral W mapping to its image W' (proof lines 3240-3250).
Conclude by the three dimension cases, using the proper integral curve over the function field of W' and the alteration lemma (proof lines 3252-3304).
difficulty_reason: The lemma is the functoriality statement that a proper morphism preserves rational equivalence, p_* alpha rationally equivalent to p_* beta whenever alpha and beta are (statement lines 3216-3223, tag 02S2). Although the statement looks formal, the proof is a real reduction: it distributes the pushforward over the locally finite family, reduces to a single integral W and its image W', and then distinguishes three dimension cases, the delicate one being dim_delta(W') = k where one must observe that the fibre over the generic point of W' is a proper integral curve over a field, that its closed points correspond to the integral subschemes through which the divisor passes, and that the multiplicity of the image class equals the multiplicity of [Spec(K)] in the pushforward of the principal divisor, which vanishes. The identification of the multiplicities is the substance, so the claim is H2.
